items.title: Google Ads Disallows Impersonate Public Figures With AI Even If Disclosed
items.description: Google Ads clarified in its unacceptable Business Practices policy that impersonating public figures using AI isn't allowed, even if they disclose that they were generated or edited using AI.

items.title: Google Ads Disallows Targeting Users Based On Prohibited Content Interests
items.description: Google Ads has added a single line to the Restricted targeting in Personalized advertising policy. Google wrote, "Additionally, advertisers are not allowed to target users based on an interest in categories prohibited in Google's ad network."

items.title: Google Ads 'Found On Site' Icon & More Pages Label On Sponsored Results
items.description: Google is testing a new label on its sponsored results on Google Ads named "Found on site." The label also has a text with a magnifying glass icon next to it. Next to the label is a site link that you can click on.

items.title: Google Ads Editor Version 2.14 Is Now Available
items.description: Google has released version 2.14 of the Google Ads Editor, which includes 10 new features.

items.title: Google Ads Data Strength Uplift Metric Doc
items.description: Google Ads has posted a new help document about the data strength uplift metric. This comes a month after Google posted another help document on Data Strength Best Practices. "The data strength uplift metric gives you a clearer picture of the value your first-party data setup delivers in Google Ads," Google wrote.

items.title: Bing Touts Two Methods To Turn Off AI In Search But It's Not A Search Setting
items.description: Microsoft announced, again, that there are ways to turn off AI features in Bing Search. We covered it twice before, but the first time we covered it, Bing had a search setting to disable AI Search (aka Copilot) from showing up in Bing. The second time, Bing removed that setting and asked people to download a browser extension or add -ai to the query to disable AI search features.

items.title: Google Placing Source Icons At Bottom Of AI Overviews
items.description: Google is testing moving the citations or sources icons to the very bottom of the AI Overviews. Previously, these icons appeared at the top of the AI Overview; now Google is testing placing them at the bottom, which may make it even harder to find the sources of the answers Google generates in these AI Overviews and could reduce clicks to your site even more.

items.title: Google Ads API Version 26.2 Now Out Available
items.description: Google Ads has just released a minor update to its Google Ads API - version 26.2. This update touches on assets, campaigns, reporting, and more general updates.

items.title: Google Search AI Overview Definitions Expanded By Default
items.description: Google is expanding the AI Overviews for definitions by default, where you no longer have to click on "Show more" to see the full version of the AI Overview. This is similar to when Google confirmed it dynamically expands some AI Overviews based on the query, but now Google is doing this for all definition searches.

items.title: Google: How Moving to a CDN Can Accidentally Overwhelm Your Website
items.description: Gary Illyes and Chery Prommawin released the final video in the Non-Canonical Cabinet series, this one is on CDNs, content delivery networks. They discuss why migrating a website to a CDN can suddenly increase Googlebot crawling activity, why this may overload your origin server, and how to avoid accidentally blocking Google's crawlers.

items.title: Google Crawled/Discovered - Currently Not Indexed A Site Quality Issue
items.description: This is not new, but hey, John Mueller from Google said it again, getting a status of Crawled/Discovered - Currently Not Indexed within Google Search Console's page indexing report may be a sign that Google doesn't think your site or those pages are high-quality enough to index.

items.title: Moving to a CDN without overwhelming your origin (or blocking Googlebot)
items.description: Deploying a Content Delivery Network (CDN) to distribute your site's assets across fast, globally distributed edge servers closer to users can be a major upgrade for any growing site: it lowers visitor latency and shields your origin server (the backend source of truth holding your original content) from heavy traffic.

items.title: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites
items.description: Today, we're announcing our plans to support a shared AI training control in robots.txt. This will help websites express their AI training preferences across multiple AI providers in a single step and is based on work from the AIPREF working group at the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). This builds on our long history of providing website owners with clear controls, including through Google-Extended, the AI training control we've offered since 2023.

items.title: New learning paths: curated YouTube playlists for Search fundamentals and Technical SEO
items.description: Over the years, the Search Central YouTube channel has published hundreds of videos across various series, from Search for Beginners and Ask Googlebot to Search Console Training and Search Off the Record. While our series structure works well for deep dives and episodic updates, we know that finding a clear, sequential learning path from scratch can sometimes be challenging.

items.title: Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console
items.description: Understanding how users find your content is crucial for any publisher or site owner. As Search evolves to include more visual and multimodal experiences, we want to ensure you have the data you need to analyze your performance.

From September 30 to October 2, 2026, the Google Search Central team is heading to the gorgeous city of Barcelona, Spain for three days of deep technical exploration, networking, and collaboration.

items.title: Search Central Live India 2026: Bengaluru, We're Coming (For Real This Time)
items.description: Remember back in March when we told our Indian community to "sit tight" while we figured out the APAC event calendar? Hopefully, you didn't take that too literally, because sitting tight for six months is probably not great for your back. In any case, you can finally stand up and stretch: Search Central Live is officially returning to India in 2026, specifically to Bengaluru!

items.title: Update to the Site Reputation Policy
items.description: In 2024, we introduced our site reputation policy to stop a practice where third-party content is published on a trusted website just to exploit that site's good reputation to rank higher in Search. This practice hurts search quality, and creates a bad experience for users.

items.title: Platform properties roll out globally, plus a new social and video performance guide
items.description: Earlier this month, we announced platform properties for Search Console, allowing you to track how your social and video posts on Instagram, TikTok, X, and YouTube perform on Google Search, Discover, and Google News. Today, platform properties are globally available to everyone.
